correctness.rationale: With no function symbols, every atom on e,x,y reduces to equality, testing x or y for square equal to e, comparing x² with y and y² with x, or comparing y with x⁻¹. Cancellation handles mixed products whose output is one of the input factors. Ordinary two-round equivalence therefore compares sets of possible pointed extension profiles, not profile multiplicities. For a nonidentity x the only non-generic second choices are e,x,x²,x⁻¹ and roots of x. The coincidence relations of the first four depend on orders 2,3,4,or ≥5. Order-three elements have a second root besides x⁻¹ for n≥5: multiply by a transposition of fixed letters if there is one 3-cycle; otherwise interleave two 3-cycles. In every nonidentity row a generic involution is supplied by a transposition other than x (x² is even), and a generic noninvolution by a 3-cycle outside x,x²,x⁻¹ and not squaring to x (at most one 3-cycle squares to a given nonidentity x). For x=e the three options are simply e, nonidentity involution, noninvolution. Thus there are no other profiles beyond the listed eight categories. Standard cycle-square parity proves a square of order four needs two 4-cycles, while the other seven types are realized in S_5 and persist by adding fixed letters. The five rank-at-most-two formulas separate the proposed classes: the fourth excludes x^k=e for k=1,2,3,4 using y=x², and the last uses two independently scoped existential tests, not a depth-three prefix. Independently computing all three-term relational atoms and equality for each first-move conjugacy type and every second move (python3 /workspace/review_checks.py 2) verified the exact classes through S_8 and pointed-type counts 1,2,3,5,7,7,7,8. This finite check corroborates, not replaces, the unbounded argument. Sharpness of 8! is within the specified family and vocabulary only.
